title: Pointwise convergence of fourfold ergodic averages for mixing transformations
main_claim: For an invertible mixing measure-preserving T, (1/N) sum f1(T^n x) f2(T^{2n} x) f3(T^{3n} x) f4(T^{4n} x) converges a.e. to the product of the integrals. The proof argues by contradiction. Selected-length laws on a suspension are built, and a class of 'channel' extensions is closed under selection through a tensor-packing estimate. The number of output roles in a nonzero correlation is maximized (at most 2), and a saturated extension plus a square/reanchoring argument then produces one more role, which contradicts maximality.

issues.location: Sec 2, Lemma lower-length; Appendix 7 (Prop ll-depth, Subsec ll-convergence)
issues.description: The fourfold deduction needs a.e. convergence of the triple averages at times {jn : j in J}, for every three-element J in {1,2,3,4}, on ARBITRARY invertible systems, because it is applied to non-mixing, non-ergodic extensions Y. That statement is itself a well-known open problem. In this paper it is supported only by an appendix that adapts the internal estimates of companion papers H (trilinear Hilbert local estimate) and P (depth-varying local estimate), and the adaptation cannot be checked here on its own. The parts that can be checked do check out: the oscillation-to-convergence step, the Host-Kra identification of limits, the mesh argument, and the coefficient table. This is a dependency risk, not a located gap.
issues.evidence: Appendix: 'the input needed here is a pointwise convergence theorem on arbitrary invertible probability preserving systems ... We obtain them by modifying the local four-linear construction in H and its extension ... in P.' Lemma lower-length: 'Neither ergodicity nor mixing is an assumption.'

issues.description: The whole argument is conditional on MixingCompanion Thm 1.1 (mixing implies mixing of all orders, i.e. Rokhlin's problem, a famous open problem). Every channel-closure and packing small-pair hypothesis uses it.
issues.evidence: 'We use [MixingCompanion, Theorem 1.1] in the following form ... (all-orders-input)'

issues.description: The Bessel/array argument excluding three output roles is redundant. Activation (Prop activation) needs only some b outside A, so r=3 would already be contradicted. The argument itself is correct.
issues.evidence: Proof of Thm main uses only r<=3 to choose b not in A.

coverage: Read Sections 1–6 in full. In the appendix I read the statement, the coordinate/coefficient subsection and the convergence subsection. The middle subsections, which adapt companions H and P, I only skimmed. I checked line by line: the selector phase witness (Psi=alpha(u)beta({t}), with u+is<3/4 so the outputs are exactly T^{in}x); the selected-law construction, its invariance and functoriality; the proper-fibre law via rwm/distal relative disjointness; Lemma relative-norm (van der Corput induction); channel-distal; and channel closure. For channel closure that covered the proper-collection mixing bound, the small-pair hypothesis with a bounded-degree obstruction graph, the density bound 0<=p*rho<=1, the leading-space Cauchy-Schwarz using the preserved two-group marginal, the residual bound tr(AB)/m^2<=1/d_m from the (d_m+1)-st eigenvalue, and the Cauchy-Schwarz sum over length classes with d_m^{-1}~k^{-3/2}. In the tensor packing proof I checked the Gaussian moment recursion and its 2q-th root arithmetic, the spectral split of R1/R2 (dimension <= sqrt d), the covering count, the contraction to the coefficient vectors v_n, the Sudakov-Fernique comparison with variance eps^2/128, and the exp(sqrt d log d)=m^{o(1)} conclusion. In Section 6 I checked the role bound, the saturation energy argument, the regrouped channel (where maximality forces the full product law), the square conditional laws (saturation at l=0 and l != b), the reanchoring lemma (substitution e'=S^{bt}e), the tower identity E[u|R]=g, the Hilbert-vector lemma, and the role identification A∪{b}. I verified the c_j coefficient table by hand.
sibling_notes: There was already a rank451 entry on the family-154 board for this same dir, reporting no_gap_found. My independent re-audit agrees with it, and my post replaced that entry. Sibling audits of the triple paper (rank443) and the slopes paper (rank300) flagged the same concern: the companion oscillation machinery does not use mixing, so it would give pointwise convergence of triple averages on all systems, which is open. This paper states that consequence explicitly (Lemma lower-length) and depends on it essentially, so the companion H/P adaptations deserve the heaviest scrutiny in this family.
